 J U D G M E N T
This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .25,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him.

Idayath Khan vs Suresh on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21061249/

sentences.text:
The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 28.01.2023 at around 03.45 p.m., the petitioner was travelling as an inmate in Autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.KA-06-AB-1077 from Dobbespet towards Gollahalli and near Kuthaghatta Cross, at Sharadha Cross-Shivagange Road, Sompura Hobli,
Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru, the driver of autorickshaw driven the auto in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the auto due to which auto got capsized.
Due to said accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter, the petitioner was shifted to PHC Dobbespet and then shifted to Hemavathi Hospital, Tumkur and then to District Hospital, Tumkur,
wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent amount towards medical, conveyance,
nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was doing Labour work and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of autorickshaw by its driver.
The respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In spite of service of notice, respondent No.1 not appeared before the tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, respondent No.2 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.2 also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.2 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.
Further, respondent No.2 admitted that they are the insurer of autorickshaw and contended that the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further the driver of autorickshaw was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Further contended that the autorickshaw was not having valid permit to ply in place of accident and as on the date of accident.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 28.01.2023 at about 03.45 p.m., near Kuthaghatta Cross, Sharadha Cross, Shivagange Road, Sompura Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District,
w h i l e h e w a s t r a v e l l i n g a s a n i n m a t e i n A u t o r i c k s h a w b e a r i n g Regn.No.KA-06-AB-1077, due to the rash and negligent driving of said vehicle by its driver?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?
If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?

Idayath Khan vs Suresh on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21061249/
2

3. What order or award?
6.
In order to prove the contentions of the petition, the petitioner himself got examined as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11 and closed his side of evidence.
On the other hand, the respondent insurance company examined its Manager as RW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4 and closed their side evidence.

7. Heard the arguments on the both the sides and perused the materials available on record.
8.

Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
 Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:-
 -:REASONS:-
9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 28.01.2023 at about 03.45 p.m., accident occurred near Kuthaghatta Cross, Sharadha Cross, Shivagange Road, Sompura Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk,
Bengaluru District, while he was travelling as an inmate in Autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.KA-06-AB-1077, due to the rash and negligent driving of said vehicle by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.
10.
In order to prove rash and negligent driving of Autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.KA-06-AB- 1077 by its driver, the son of petitioner got examined as PW.1.
In the chief examination, PW.1 deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of autorickshaw by its driver, the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW.1, nothing has been elicited from PW.1 to disprove or disbelieve the case of petitioner.
Nothing to dispute or rebut the contention of petitioner related to the accident and cause of accident could be elicited during the cross examination.

11. Further, in order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the petitioner produced Ex.P.7, first information statement, which discloses that brother of petitioner by name Sri.Asim Pasha S/o.Basha lodged the complaint with the police on 29.01.2023 pertaining to the accident occurred on 28.01.2023.

On the basis of first information lodged by brother of petitioner, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 &
304(A) of IPC and U/s.187 of M.V.Act.
In the complaint as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of autorickshaw by its driver.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar and sketch, which are marked as Ex.P.8 & 9.

The said documents disclose that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is Idayath Khan vs Suresh on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21061249/
3 described in the said document.

entities.text: Idayath Khan vs Suresh on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that the facts at place of accident, as described in mahazar and sketch, are contrary to actual facts.
Ex.P.10 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to the vehicle are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The driver or owner of the offending vehicle not provided satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which damages are caused to the vehicles.
The driver or owner of rickshaw not provided proper explanation regarding the manner in which damages were caused to the vehicle, if the vehicle was not involved in the accident.
The said document clearly indicates involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
Ex.P.1 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.

The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279, 338 & 304(A)
of IPC and U/s.187 of M.V.Act, which is marked as Ex.P.11.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
12. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
On perusal of record, it discloses that negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle resulted in accident.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 and P.6 to P.11, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.KA-06-AB-1077 by its driver and same has resulted in injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In view of holding issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance.
14. The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained grievous injuries and underwent surgery of left shoulder dislocation and other injuries.

In order to prove the injuries, petitioner has produced Ex.P.1 - wound certificate issued by District Hospital, Tumkur, wherein the doctor diagnosed the petitioner and stated that the petitioner sustained dislocation of left shoulder and blister on right palm and opined that the injuries are simple in nature.

The petitioner produced Idayath Khan vs Suresh on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21061249/
4 Ex.P.2 - discharge summary issued by District Hospital, Tumakuru, wherein doctor diagnosed that petitioner sustained fracture of left shoulder dislocation and took treatment as an inpatient from 28.01.2023 to 30.01.2023 i.e., a period of three days.
In order to prove the disability, the petitioner neither produced disability certificate nor examined the doctor.
The petitioner not furnished satisfactory materials in order to ascertain and adjudicate the aspect of disability, as contended by him.
The petitioner has produced medical bills which are marked as Ex.P.4 and the bills amount to a sum of .1,500/- and medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.3.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut the medical bills furnished by petitioner.
No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to controvert or rebut the bills furnished by petitioner.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove the aspect of disability.
The petitioner not furnished satisfactory materials in order to substantiate his contentions related to disability and also to substantiate his contention related to occupation and income.
The petitioner also not furnished satisfactory materials to show that he sustained loss of income and lost his earning capacity due to accidental injuries.
So, in the absence of proper evidence, this tribunal cannot award compensation under the head of future loss of income and other heads.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner,
the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of .75,000/- (including medical bills).
15.

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs.
Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

sentences.text: 16. The materials on record reveals that respondent No.1 is the owner of offending Autorickshaw and the autorickshaw is having valid policy of insurance at the time of accident.

The respondent No.2 specifically contended that the offending vehicle is not having valid permit to ply over the area of accident and violated the terms of policy conditions and hence, they are not liable to pay compensation.

In order to substantiate the said contention, the respondent No.2 furnished certified copy of permit and B-Register Extract pertaining to offending vehicle, which are marked as Ex.R.3 &
4.

On perusal of Ex.R.3, it could be noticed that permit with respect to the offending vehicle is given by Regional Transport Authority, Tumkur and permission pertains to movement of vehicle within the radius of 10 Kms in the Town Municipal limits of Tumkur.
As per Ex.R3, the offending vehicle is having permit valid from 25.03.2018 to 24.03.2023, but the permit is limited to ply the vehicle within the radius of 10 kms in town Municipal limits of Tumkur.
As per the materials on record, the accident took place at Dabaspet which falls within the jurisdiction of Nelamangala.
The offending vehicle does not appear to have permit to ply the vehicle within the limits of Nelamangala.
Ex.R3 does not disclose the aspect of grant of permit to respondent No.1 to ply the vehicle within the limits of Nelamangala.
Ex.R3 reveals the aspect of offending vehicle not having permit to ply the vehicle within the limits of Nelamangala where the accident took place.
The petitioner not produced any materials contrary to Ex.R3.
The petitioner also not furnished the materials to show that the offending vehicle was having valid permit to ply the vehicle within the limits of Nelamangala.

Further, Ex.R4 - B-Register Extract pertaining to the offending vehicle, reflects the aspect of grant of permit to ply the vehicle within the radius of 15 kms Nelamangala limits of Tumkur, but the offending vehicle travelled beyond the limits to which permit is being granted.

The materials on Idayath Khan vs Suresh on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21061249/
5 record do not disclose the aspect of possessing permit to ply the vehicle within the limits of Nelamangala.

entities.text: Idayath Khan vs Suresh on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ex.R3 & 4 clearly discloses the aspect of granting of permit to ply the vehicle only within the limits of Tumkur Municipal limits Corporation upto the radius of 15 Kms.
It is not forthcoming for the materials on record related to permit being granted for plying the vehicle in the jurisdiction of Nelamangala.
Ex.R3 & 4 substantiates the contention of respondent No.2 regarding plying of vehicle outside the area to which permit was granted.
There is violation of conditions mentioned in the permit by the driver of offending vehicle.
As there is violation of conditions related to permit, the said violation falls under Sec.150 of M.V.Act.
As per Sec.150 of M.V.Act, the insurance company can plead the defence related to violation of permit among other grounds provided under the said provision.
The materials on record clearly disclose the aspect of violation of conditions of permit as well as conditions of policy of insurance by respondent No.1.
It is pertinent to note that respondent No.1 not appeared before the tribunal in order to negate the contention of respondent No.2.

Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 neither appeared nor placed materials to show that the offending vehicle was having valid and effective permit to ply in the area of accident as on the date of accident.

The materials placed on record disclose the aspect of violation of conditions of permit by respondent No.1.
17.
The accident in question occurred on 28.01.2023 i.e., subsequent to the amendment which came into effect from 1/4/2022.
As per the provisions of Sec.150 of Motor Vehicles, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability to pay compensation if there is violation of terms of the policy.

In the present case, the driver of Autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.KA-06-AB-1077 does not appear to have valid permit to drive the vehicle which aspect is forthcoming from the materials placed on record.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of violation of terms of the policy.

Though the policy pertaining to offending vehicle is in existence at the time of accident, as there is violation of conditions of permit, the insurance company cannot be held liable to pay the compensation.

Further, in view of the amendment to the Act, as discussed supra, no liability can be fastened on the Respondent No.2, to pay the compensation and to recover the same from the Respondent No.1 under pay and recovery theory.

18. The counsel for respondent No.2 relied on the decisions mentioned below in support of their contention:
1. ILR 2012 KAR 6065 of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in between Sri.B.T.Venkatesh Vs. Sri.Jagadeesh Kumar and others.
2. MFA.No.967 of 2017 (MV-D) of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in between Sri.Venkatesh Vs. IFFCO Tokio Gen Insurance CO., Ltd., and others.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sri.Venkatesh Vs. IFFCO Tokio Gen Insurance CO., Ltd., and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 19. This Tribunal carefully considered the said decisions and said decisions are applicable to the case on hand.

Accordingly, the Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the liability of paying the compensation to the petitioners is to be fastened solely on the Respondent No.1, who is the owner of the offending vehicle, as he has violated the policy condition by plying the vehicle in the limits to which permit was not valid and effective.
The offending vehicle does not have permit to ply in the limits in which accident occurred.

Respondent No.1 not appeared before the Tribunal in order to Idayath Khan vs Suresh on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21061249/
6 controvert the contention of petitioner as well as respondent No.2.
Respondent No.1 neither appeared nor placed materials to show that the vehicle involved in the accident was taken without his permission or knowledge.
Respondent No.1 not appeared before the court and also not put forth any contention contrary to the version of petitioner and respondent No.2.
There is violation of terms of the policy issued by respondent No.2.
As there is violation of terms of the policy, the liability cannot be fastened on respondent No.2 to pay the compensation.
Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.2 is answered Partly in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 is solely liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest within two months from the date of award.
This petition against the Respondent No.2 is dismissed.
Entire compensation amount shall be released in favour of petitioner as amount is meager one.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer over computer, corrected and pronounced by me in open court on this 05th day of May, 2025.)
(NARENDRA.B.R) I ADDL.
